name: GitHub
one_liner: Code hosting platform exposing repositories, pull requests, issues, and Actions through REST and GraphQL APIs.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens (fine-grained or classic) and GitHub App tokens sent as Authorization: Bearer; OAuth apps use authorization code and device flow; GitHub Apps authenticate with JWT then installation tokens; GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions.
access_notes: Any account can create a PAT, OAuth app or GitHub App self-serve; authenticated limit is 5,000 req/h (15,000 on Enterprise Cloud-owned apps). Marketplace listing review is optional, not required for API use.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve PATs, OAuth apps and GitHub Apps, documented REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks, and an official hosted MCP server. Endpoint count not verified but surface is plainly large.

auth.quote: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions workflow.
GitHub's OAuth implementation supports the standard authorization code grant type and the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant

access.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

api_surface.quote: The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour.
Webhooks let you subscribe to events happening in a software system and automatically receive a delivery of data to your server

mcp.quote: The remote GitHub MCP Server is hosted by GitHub and provides the easiest method for getting up and running.

disputes.why: Docs show PATs and GitHub App tokens as Bearer, plus App JWT and OAuth code/device flows.
Large REST and GraphQL surface across repos, issues, PRs, Actions; exact count not verified.
github/github-mcp-server is vendor org repo; remote server hosted by GitHub. First-pass URL was a third-party Algolia link.
Official remote MCP endpoint per vendor repo README.
No app review needed to create OAuth apps or GitHub Apps; none found in docs.
